title: Console: validate + harden audit log export destination configuration workflows
creator: Dylan Brooks
project: Audit logging schema standardization + 100% sensitive-action coverage
description:
Problem
Enterprise customers (especially Private) are configuring audit log exports to Splunk HEC / Azure Sentinel / generic HTTPS sinks. Misconfigurations are common (bad URL, TLS issues, wrong auth header, invalid workspace IDs, rate limits) and current Console workflows make it easy to: (a) save a broken config, (b) unintentionally disable exports, or (c) leak secrets via UI/logging. We also need to ensure changes to export config are always audited (sensitive action coverage) with consistent actor attribution.

Goal
Add Console-side validation + safer workflows for configuring export destinations so misconfigurations are prevented early and every change is audited. Provide a predictable operator experience across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and avoid introducing secret/PII leakage.

Non-goals
- Building a full audit log viewer UI.
- Implementing new exporter targets (handled in ENG-4836 / exporter repo).
- Replacing backend validation/normalization (this ticket complements exporter validation; it does not substitute).

Scope
Console UI + Console backend API surfaces used by the UI for:
- Create export destination
- Update export destination
- Rotate credentials / update auth material
- Enable/disable exports
- Test connection / send test event
- Delete export destination

Key requirements
1) Validation (client + server)
- URL validation: enforce https://, disallow localhost/loopback/link-local/private ranges by default (Private deployments can allow via explicit toggle / policy), block obvious typos.
- Auth validation: required fields per destination type (e.g., Splunk HEC token required; Sentinel workspace + key required; generic HTTPS header name/value rules).
- TLS validation: warn on insecure settings; require explicit acknowledgement if allowing custom CA / skipping verification (Private only; gated behind admin setting).
- Rate limit / batching parameters: enforce min/max; guardrails to prevent extreme drop risk.
- Data residency warnings: if destination region differs from tenant residency setting, show a warning with link to docs (do not block; product decision).
- Field cardinality / custom tags: restrict free-form dimensions (allow-list keys; cap length).

2) Safe workflows
- Two-step flow: (a) Configure (draft) -> (b) Validate/Test -> (c) Apply.
- “Test connection” must not persist secrets in logs or in browser storage. Use ephemeral test request to backend.
- “Send test event” uses a synthetic audit event (event_type=AUDIT_LOG_EXPORT.TEST) with clear marker test_event=true and no tenant secrets.
- Update workflow shows a diff summary (what will change) before apply.
- Credential rotation flow separated from non-secret fields; secret fields are write-only and never re-rendered.
- Disable/delete requires explicit confirmation and displays impact (export will stop; events still retained per retention policy).

3) Auditing requirements
- Every create/update/rotate/enable/disable/delete/test action emits canonical v1 audit event(s) with correct actor attribution.
- Required correlation fields included (request_id/trace_id/admin_action_id) per ENG-4830.
- UI should pass an idempotency key (admin_action_id) to backend for retries, so duplicate UI clicks don’t create duplicate state transitions.

4) UX + accessibility
- Clear inline errors mapped to backend error codes.
- Copy should be actionable (“Check Splunk HEC endpoint path (/services/collector) and token permissions.”).
- Prevent foot-guns: don’t allow saving an untested destination unless explicitly bypassed (with audit event for bypass).

5) Security / privacy
- Secrets are masked; never show full tokens/keys after save.
- Prevent secrets in Console logs/telemetry (verify redaction for network errors).
- Ensure we don’t log full destination URLs if query params could contain secrets; strip query params in UI logging.

Implementation notes
- Console backend should be the source of truth for validation; UI performs pre-checks for fast feedback.
- Define stable error codes from backend: EXPORT_DEST_INVALID_URL, EXPORT_DEST_TLS_ERROR, EXPORT_DEST_AUTH_INVALID, EXPORT_DEST_TEST_TIMEOUT, EXPORT_DEST_BLOCKED_IP_RANGE, etc.
- “Test connection” should call a dedicated endpoint that:
  - validates config
  - attempts handshake/auth
  - returns structured result
  - does NOT persist the destination unless Apply is called
- Add a feature flag for Private: allow_insecure_tls and allow_private_ips (default false).

Acceptance criteria
- Cannot save export destination with invalid URL/auth; UI blocks and shows clear message.
- Test connection required before Apply (unless bypass with explicit confirmation).
- All export config changes produce v1 audit events (validated by schema validator) and appear in coverage dashboard as observed.
- Secret fields are never returned by backend after creation/update; UI never displays them.
- E2E tests cover: create+test+apply, update non-secret, rotate secret, disable/enable, delete, bypass test (if allowed), and error handling.

Rollout plan
- Phase 1: Add backend validation + error codes and wire into UI forms (feature flag).
- Phase 2: Add test connection + synthetic test event.
- Phase 3: Enforce “test before apply” and add bypass auditing.
- Phase 4: Enable by default for Hosted/Dedicated; coordinate with Private installer docs for flags.

Links / references
- Confluence: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/audit-log-events-logging-standard.json
- Project PRD draft: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/product/security-and-compliance/audit-logging-prd-draft.json
- Customer requirements: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/security-and-compliance/customer-siem-export-requirements.json
- Related tickets: ENG-4827 (exporter normalization), ENG-4825 (console backend audit events), ENG-4836 (SIEM targets)

Open questions
- Should “destination region mismatch” be a hard block for some tenants (regulated) or warning only?
- Private: do we allow non-https endpoints inside the customer network (default no; needs explicit override)?
- Do we require “test connection” on every edit, or only when changing connectivity/auth fields?

Requested reviewers
- Kevin Osei (exporter behavior + SIEM semantics)
- Naomi Feldman (PM / external messaging constraints)
- Michael Grant (privacy/legal review for data residency warnings)
- Allison Grant (observability standards)
comments: 2026-02-13 (Felix Schneider): Did quick audit of current Console flow. We currently persist config immediately on “Save”, then show a generic toast on exporter errors later. Need restructure to draft/test/apply as described. I’ll propose UI states + backend endpoints in a short design note for review in #eng-security.

2026-02-14 (Kevin Osei): Strongly recommend backend owns validation + test connection. Exporter will reject invalid configs, but Console should prevent broken config from being stored. Also please ensure test event uses schema_version and a deterministic event_type for customer filtering.

2026-02-17 (Chloe Martin): Backend API changes: proposing POST /audit-exports/validate (no persistence) and POST /audit-exports/test (no persistence, optional send_test_event). Apply remains POST/PUT /audit-exports. Secret fields write-only. Will add error codes so UI can map to messages.

2026-02-19 (Naomi Feldman): On test bypass: we can allow bypass only for Private, behind admin setting. Must emit explicit audit event when bypassed (customer asked for this in security reviews). Also avoid promising cross-region blocking until we align with residency policy.

2026-02-21 (Allison Grant): Please strip query params in any client-side telemetry. Also ensure we don’t add high-cardinality fields like raw error strings into audit events. Put detailed diagnostics in internal logs with redaction, and return normalized error codes to UI.

2026-02-24 (Felix Schneider): Implemented UI draft: wizard w/ steps Configure -> Validate -> Apply. Waiting on backend error code contract. Added copy variants for Splunk and Sentinel. Next: integrate correlation admin_action_id and add confirm dialogs for disable/delete.

2026-02-26 (Dylan Brooks): Flagging dependency risk: if ENG-4825 backend auditing lands late, we still need UI shipped behind feature flag, but we cannot GA until audit events for export config are emitted and validated. Please keep this ticket aligned with ENG-4825 PR sequencing.
